programs.name: `scaffold-project.cjs`
programs.what: Checks that a project's folders exist, and creates any that are missing. It never deletes, moves or overwrites anything, and it creates nothing when the project folder holds things the layout does not know.
takesIn: an EPIC, a change or a section, when that piece needs its own folder
givesOut: the project's folders, such as sources/, frd/ and epics/
a piece's own folder, such as an EPIC's folder or a change's folder, when you name it
a message, and nothing created, when the project folder holds things the layout does not know
inFlow: `stories-workflow`, at the start of each EPIC
`epic-author` in register mode, before anything is written
`frd-author`, before it creates the FRD file
`epic-author` in brief mode, with the EPIC, to create the EPIC's folder
`requirement-update-workflow` step 1, with the change, to create the change's folder
you can run it any time. Running it again changes no folder or file that already exists
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Every workflow and author skill runs it at the start, in the forward flow.

programs.name: `accept.cjs`
programs.what: Does everything that must happen when you accept a document, in a fixed order, and stops at the first step that fails. It saves the version, rebuilds the Traceability map and brings every open change up to date.
takesIn: the document being accepted, such as brd, frd or story-list
the piece it belongs to, when it has one: a capability, an EPIC, a story or a change
givesOut: a numbered copy of the document in the Version log, and its status line set to accepted, through `version-log.cjs`
a numbered copy of the data model's decisions file, when the document is the things file or a data model file
a numbered copy of the Question log, when the project has one and it is not the document being accepted
the Traceability map rebuilt, through `traceability-map.cjs`
every open change's progress updated, through `track-change.cjs`
pass, or the exit code of the first step that failed
inFlow: `discovery-author`, when you accept the Discovery brief
`glossary-author`, last, to save the Glossary gate log
`things-author`, when you accept the things file
`data-model-author`, when you accept a data model file
`feature-author`, when you accept the Feature catalog
`epic-grouping-author`, when you accept the EPIC grouping
`epic-author` in brief mode, when you accept the EPIC brief
`epic-author` in register mode, when `check-register.cjs` passes, because a pass is the EPIC register's acceptance
`glossary-disposition`, last, to save the Glossary gate log
`insert-answer.cjs`, for each accepted document it changes
`copy-wording.cjs`, for each accepted document it changes
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Every gate in the forward flow runs it when you accept.

programs.name: `version-log.cjs`
programs.what: Saves a numbered copy of a document the moment you accept it. It sets the document's status line to "accepted on {date}, version {n}" and adds one row to the Version log.
takesIn: the document, by its name or its path inside the project
the piece it belongs to, when it has one: a capability, an EPIC, a story or a change
givesOut: the document's status line set to accepted, with its version number: a Story has no status line
a copy of the document in version-log/, as v{n}.md
one new row in the Version log, version-log/log.md, with the document's latest Decision record entry
inFlow: `accept.cjs`, at every acceptance: once for the document, once for the data model's decisions file when it applies, and once for the Question log
programs.changeOnlyWhy: `accept.cjs` runs it at every acceptance in the forward flow.

programs.name: `traceability-map.cjs`
programs.what: Rebuilds the Traceability map from the latest accepted version of each document. It lists links whose far end is missing, as waiting when that document is not accepted yet, or as a problem when it is.
takesIn: the Version log, to find the latest accepted copy of each document
every accepted document, the things file and the data model files among them
givesOut: traceability-map.json, the Traceability map
pass, or the problems found: missing links and IDs that appear twice
inFlow: `find-linked.cjs` and `recommend.cjs` load its readers, so they read documents the same way
programs.changeOnlyWhy: `accept.cjs` runs it at every acceptance in the forward flow.

programs.name: `track-change.cjs`
programs.what: Keeps each open change's progress up to date. It writes the change's progress file from the option you chose at the change's gate, marks each document accepted once a later version is saved, and closes the change when every document is accepted.
takesIn: each accepted Change impact report whose progress is not closed
givesOut: changes/{change}/progress.md, written when the change has no progress yet
each progress row marked accepted once its document has a later version
the change closed, through `close-change.cjs`, when every row is accepted
nothing to do, when no change is open
programs.changeOnlyWhy: `accept.cjs` runs it at every acceptance, in the forward flow too. It only has work to do while a change is open.

programs.name: `status.cjs`
programs.what: Says where a project stands and what to run next. It prints one line per step and piece, the open changes, the open Must answer questions, the open entries in the data model's decisions file, and a "Next:" line.
takesIn: the status line of every document
the data model's things file and decisions file
the latest accepted Feature catalog and EPIC register
givesOut: one line per step and piece: not started, drafted, accepted, parked, ready or written
the open changes
every Must answer question still open
every entry still open in the data model's decisions file
"Next:", the next thing to run, with parked pieces last
inFlow: `things-author`, at its start, to find the entries still open that it must ask again
`data-model-author`, at its start, to find the entries still open that it must ask again
`frd-workflow`, which follows what it names for an accepted FRD that waits on a data model answer now settled
you can run it any time. It changes nothing
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Every author skill in the forward flow closes with it.

programs.name: `grade-questions.cjs`
programs.what: Places every question in the Question log in its group, sets the order they are asked in, and checks the log. It also checks that every gap in the project's documents names a question that is in the log.
takesIn: the grid in the Question log template
every document in the project, for the gaps that name a question
givesOut: the Question log's four group sections rewritten in the right order: nothing changed with --check-only
three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
pass, or the problems found. An open question is never a problem
inFlow: every author skill except the data model's two, after `probing-questions-author` raises the questions and before the gate
its "For the person" block is shown at each gate, after the check program's
`status.cjs`, which reads its results and changes nothing
`insert-answer.cjs`, which finds the gaps that name a question the same way
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Every author skill in the forward flow runs it before its gate.

programs.name: `check-simple-writing.cjs`
programs.what: Checks one or more documents against the simple writing rules, and says what to fix and what to look at. It is the quick check for a document that has no check program of its own, such as a Glossary page or the Question log.
takesIn: the project name, so the agreed Glossary words are allowed
columns to skip, and a pair of columns to compare, when asked
givesOut: pass, or what to fix
what to look at, such as sentences over 20 words
inFlow: `probing-questions-author`, on the Question log, after it writes
`glossary-author`, before each gate and before finishing
`glossary-disposition`, on each glossary page it changed and the Glossary gate log
`data-model-workflow`, on the decision register after each mark it writes
`adversarial-check`, on the Change impact report after it writes section 11
`feature-impact`, when it writes its block into a file itself
any skill, after writing a file that has no check program
you can run it any time, on any document
programs.changeOnlyWhy: `probing-questions-author`, `glossary-author` and `data-model-workflow` run it in the forward flow.

programs.name: `lib/run-paths.cjs`
programs.what: Turns a project and a document name into the document's path, from the one copy of the folder layout in project-folders.md. It also holds the shared helpers for reading command options, reading and writing text, and stopping with an error.
takesIn: a document name, with its values such as an EPIC or a capability
givesOut: the document's path, and whether the file exists
which document a path is
the folders to create at setup
inFlow: loaded by every program in tools/
named by `frd-author` as the way it finds its files
named by `change-impact-author` as the way it finds its files
named by `probing-questions-author` as the way it finds the Question log
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Every program loads it.

programs.name: `lib/md-tables.cjs`
programs.what: Reads the markdown tables under a given heading into rows keyed by column name. It also reads a Story's acceptance scenarios and the rule IDs each one names.
givesOut: every heading in the document
the rows of every table under the heading
a Story's scenarios, each with the rules it proves
inFlow: loaded by the three route programs
loaded by `lib/check-document.cjs` and the other libraries
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Programs of the forward flow load it.

programs.name: `lib/check-document.cjs`
programs.what: Holds the checks every check program shares, and prints the three blocks a gate needs: For the person, One line, and For the file. It checks the opening, the template's sections, placeholders left in, markdown that will not render and simple writing.
givesOut: the shared check results, each a name and its findings
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: loaded by the three route programs
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Every check program of the forward flow loads it.

programs.name: `lib/md-lint.cjs`
programs.what: Finds markdown that will not render as written. Examples are a table row with the wrong number of cells, text in angle brackets, a link path with a space, and a broken mermaid diagram.
givesOut: a list of problems, each with its line, or nothing when the text renders cleanly
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Every check program of the forward flow runs it.

programs.name: `lib/simple-writing.cjs`
programs.what: Checks a document against the simple writing rules. It lists what to fix, such as a hard word or a semicolon, and what to look at, such as a sentence over 20 words.
takesIn: the simple writing rules' word lists
the agreed Glossary words, which it never flags
columns to skip, and a pair of columns to compare, when asked
givesOut: what to fix, each one a finding
what to look at, shown at the gate
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Every check program of the forward flow runs it.

programs.name: `lib/one-per-row.cjs`
programs.what: Lists the rows that may hold two requirements, such as a rule with two actions joined by "and". It never fails a row, because only you can judge it: each row is shown to look at.
takesIn: the rows a check program gives it, each with its ID, its text and its kind
givesOut: each row that may hold two requirements, to look at
the lines the gate shows in For the person
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Check programs of the forward flow run it.

programs.name: `lib/scan-retired-words.cjs`
programs.what: Finds the words the Glossary retired that a document still uses, and names the agreed word to use now. It skips the kit's own words, quotes, code, IDs and the Decision record.
takesIn: a document's text and the name of its template
the "Terms replaced or retired over time" tables on the Glossary's four kind pages
givesOut: each retired word used, with its line and the word to use now
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Check programs of the forward flow run it.

programs.name: `lib/data-model.cjs`
programs.what: Reads a product's data model: the things file, the data model file of each family it names, and the data model's decisions file. Every program that needs the data model reads it through this library, so they all read it the same way.
takesIn: each data model file the things file names
givesOut: the whole data model as data: families, things, actions, fields and moves
every entry in the data model's decisions file, open and settled
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Programs of the forward flow load it, such as `check-data-model.cjs` and `check-features.cjs`.

programs.name: `list-sources.cjs`
programs.what: Lists every file in a project's sources/ folder, and marks the files that are the same as another or an older version of another. This way no file is missed or counted twice.
givesOut: "For the brief": the counts and one table per folder, in the shape of the Discovery brief's section 1
"For discovery-author": the files whose names differ only by a date, for you to judge, or "None"
inFlow: `check-discovery-brief.cjs` loads it, to check section 1 of the Discovery brief
programs.changeOnlyWhy: `discovery-author` runs it at the start of the forward flow.

programs.name: `check-discovery-brief.cjs`
programs.what: Checks the Discovery brief before its gate, and prints the three blocks the gate needs. It checks that section 1 lists every source file once, that every clash is settled, and that every Silent topic and assumption names its question.
givesOut: pass, or the problems found
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: `discovery-author`, before its gate "Accept the Discovery brief?", in step 1 of `requirements-workflow`. It is run again until every check passes
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the check of the first forward step.

programs.name: `check-brd.cjs`
programs.what: Checks the BRD before its gate, and prints the three blocks the gate needs. It checks the template's sections, that business requirements run from BR-01 with no gaps, that every KPI has a confidence tag, and that every line says where it came from.
givesOut: pass, or the problems found
business requirements that may hold two actions, to look at
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: `brd-author`, before its gate "Accept the BRD?", in step 2 of `requirements-workflow`. It is run again until every check passes
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the check of a forward step.

programs.name: `check-prd.cjs`
programs.what: Checks the PRD before its gate, and prints the three blocks the gate needs. It checks that every requirement has its ID, its wording and its source, traces to business requirements in the BRD, and holds one requirement per row.
takesIn: the requirement files in sources/, to compare the client's words
the Glossary, when the project has one
givesOut: pass, or the problems found
requirements that may hold two actions, to look at
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: `prd-author`, before its gate "Accept the PRD?", in step 3 of `requirements-workflow`. It is run again until every check passes
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the check of a forward step.

programs.name: `fill-also-written-as.cjs`
programs.what: Before Gate 2 of the Glossary is shown, fills each Gate 2 row's "Also written as" from the settled Gate 1 rows. The words a term replaces are copied by a program, never retyped.
takesIn: the Glossary gate log, its Gate 1 rows and any Re-run part
givesOut: the "Also written as" column of each Gate 2 row, filled. No other cell changes
nothing written, and the open rows listed, while a Gate 1 row is still open
programs.changeOnlyWhy: `glossary-author` runs it when the Glossary is built in the forward flow.

programs.name: `build-glossary-records.cjs`
programs.what: Builds the decision register and every section decisions file from the Glossary gate log, the only place a glossary decision is written. It gives each settled row a decision ID, D-1 onward.
givesOut: the table under "The register" in glossary/decision-register.md
glossary/deep-dives/{section}/{section}-decisions.md for every section
nothing written, and the open rows listed, while a gate-log row is still open
inFlow: `glossary-author`, when it writes its output, after both gates are closed
`glossary-disposition`, after it records a glossary change
`fill-also-written-as.cjs` and `build-retired-words-tables.cjs` load it, to read the gate log the same way
programs.changeOnlyWhy: `glossary-author` runs it when the Glossary is built in the forward flow.

programs.name: `build-retired-words-tables.cjs`
programs.what: Writes the "Terms replaced or retired over time" table on each of the Glossary's four kind pages, from the Glossary gate log. The table is never edited by hand.
givesOut: the "Terms replaced or retired over time" table on each kind page, or "None yet."
nothing written, and the open rows listed, while a gate-log row is still open
inFlow: `glossary-disposition`, after it records a glossary change
programs.changeOnlyWhy: `glossary-author` runs it when the Glossary is built in the forward flow.

programs.name: `check-data-model.cjs`
programs.what: Checks the data model before its gate, and prints the three blocks the gate needs. Without a family it checks the things file. With a family it checks that one data model file. It checks the data model's decisions file every time.
takesIn: the things file, or one data model file named by its family
givesOut: pass, or the problems found
rows that may hold two requirements, to look at
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: `things-author`, before its gate, in step 1 of `data-model-workflow`
`data-model-author`, with the family, before its gate, in step 2 of `data-model-workflow`
both again in step 4 of `data-model-workflow`, for terms the Glossary changed
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the check of the data model's forward steps.

programs.name: `check-features.cjs`
programs.what: Checks the Feature catalog before its gate, and prints the three blocks the gate needs. It checks that every requirement in the PRD lands in a feature, that every "Done when" is cut into pieces, and that every action and move in the data model files has its feature.
takesIn: the things file and every data model file it names
givesOut: pass, or the problems found
data model rows still waiting on a feature or a change, listed for you
feature names and descriptions that may hold two things, to look at
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: `feature-author`, before its gate "Accept the Feature catalog?", in step 1 of `features-and-epics-workflow`. It is run again until every check passes
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the check of a forward step.

programs.name: `check-epic-grouping.cjs`
programs.what: Checks the EPIC grouping before its gate, and prints the three blocks the gate needs. It checks the two or three options, that the chosen grouping is copied in full, and it finds every clash from the Feature catalog so none is missed.
givesOut: pass, or the problems found, every clash not yet settled among them
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: `epic-grouping-author`, before its gate "Pick a grouping, settle its clashes, confirm the EPIC brief list", in step 2 of `features-and-epics-workflow`
`epic-grouping-author`, in a change, after it places one new feature
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the check of a forward step.

programs.name: `check-register.cjs`
programs.what: Proves the EPIC register is an exact copy of the chosen grouping in the EPIC grouping, and checks its simple writing. The EPIC register has no gate: a pass is its acceptance.
givesOut: pass, or each mismatch and each simple writing problem
the date written on the register's "Copy checked on" line, on a pass
inFlow: `epic-author` in register mode, in step 3 of `features-and-epics-workflow`. On a mismatch the copy is corrected and it is run again, and on a pass `accept.cjs` runs
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the check of a forward step.

programs.name: `build-sequencing-mapping.cjs`
programs.what: Builds the EPIC sequencing and the EPIC mapping from the EPIC register, so neither is written by hand. It works out each EPIC's step, the critical path and the most depended-on EPIC, and checks that every feature is in exactly one EPIC.
givesOut: the EPIC sequencing, epics/sequencing.md
the EPIC mapping, epics/mapping.md
a dependency loop, or a feature not in exactly one EPIC, listed. Nothing is written for a loop
inFlow: step 4 of `features-and-epics-workflow`, after the EPIC register is accepted. A loop sends the run back to step 2
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is a step of the forward flow.

programs.name: `route-next-capability.cjs`
programs.what: Names the next FRD to write. It orders the capabilities by the EPIC register's run order, leaves out the accepted ones, and puts those waiting on a Must answer question, then the parked ones, last.
givesOut: the next capability and its features, then the queue
or "Every FRD accepted: next, run stories-workflow."
inFlow: step 1 of `frd-workflow`, at the start of each run
`frd-workflow` again at the end, to print what comes next
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the first step of `frd-workflow`.

takesIn: the things file, the data model files and the data model's decisions file
givesOut: pass, or the problems found
rules that may hold two behaviours, to look at
the FRD guard: each open Must answer question the FRD names, and a line saying it cannot be accepted until it is answered or parked
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: `frd-author`, before its gate "Accept the FRD?" and after every decision, in step 2 of `frd-workflow`
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the check of a forward step.

programs.what: Sets a piece in progress aside, at the back of the queue, by setting its status line to parked. It parks an FRD or an EPIC at its gate, or every FRD and EPIC in progress when a change is Large.
takesIn: a capability, to park that FRD
or an EPIC, to park that EPIC
or a change, to park every FRD and EPIC in progress
for a change: section 14 of its Change impact report, and the pieces in progress, through `size-rules.cjs`

a message, and nothing parked, when nothing is in progress or the change is not Large
inFlow: `frd-author`, at its gate, when you choose to park after your third "no", or while a Must answer question is open
at an EPIC's gates, after your third "no", when you choose "Park it"
step 6 of `requirement-update-workflow`, when the change is Large and you chose to run the path. `change-impact-author` names it first in the path
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is also used at an FRD's or an EPIC's gate after your third "no", in the forward flow.

programs.name: `route-next-epic.cjs`
programs.what: Names the next EPIC to write stories for. It follows the EPIC register's run order, leaves out the EPICs that are ready, and puts last those waiting on a Must answer question, the parked ones, and those that depend on a parked one.
takesIn: every Story list and its Stories
givesOut: the next EPIC, then the queue
or "Every EPIC ready."
inFlow: step 1 of `stories-workflow`, at the start of each run
`stories-workflow` again at the end, to print what comes next
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the first step of `stories-workflow`.

programs.name: `route-brief-list.cjs`
programs.what: Says whether an EPIC gets an EPIC brief, from the EPIC brief list in the EPIC grouping. It prints yes or no, then the reason the list gives.
takesIn: the EPIC grouping's EPIC brief list
givesOut: "yes" or "no" on the first line
the reason the list gives
inFlow: step 2 of `stories-workflow`: on yes, `epic-author` runs in brief mode. On no, the workflow goes to `story-drafter`

programs.name: `check-epic-brief.cjs`
programs.what: Checks an EPIC brief before its gate, and prints the three blocks the gate needs. It checks that the brief matches its EPIC register row and the Feature catalog, and that every measure has a confidence tag.
givesOut: pass, or the problems found
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: `epic-author` in brief mode, before its gate "Accept the EPIC brief?", in step 3 of `stories-workflow`
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It is the check of a forward step.

programs.name: `check-stories.cjs`
programs.what: Checks an EPIC's Story list and Stories before each story gate, and prints the three blocks the gate needs. What it checks grows with each story's stage: drafted, groomed or ready.
takesIn: the EPIC's Story list and Stories
givesOut: pass, or the problems found
stories and scenarios that may hold two actions, to look at
the ready guard: the stories cannot be ready while a Must answer question raised in them is open
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file

programs.what: Proves that every rule of an EPIC's features is named by at least one acceptance scenario. It lists every rule no scenario names.

the FRDs, for those features' rules
the EPIC's Stories, for the rule IDs each scenario names

programs.name: `reader-copy.cjs`
programs.what: Prints the copy of a document that a reader outside the kit sees, such as the body of a story's GitHub issue. It leaves out the opening notes, lines in italics and citations, and never changes the document.

givesOut: the reader's copy, printed. Nothing is written
inFlow: you, when you put a ready story into a tracker, such as a GitHub issue, as `stories-workflow` describes
you can run it any time, on any document

programs.name: `compare-versions.cjs`
programs.what: Lists every difference between a new and an old version of a requirement file, so no quiet edit is missed. It compares requirement by requirement when the files hold requirement IDs, and line by line otherwise.

a text copy beside any Word or PDF file
givesOut: section 3 of the Change impact report, "Other differences in a new version": one row per difference, or one line when nothing differs

every document drafted since it was last accepted, the things file and data model files among them

or, when an ID in section 6 is in no document, that ID listed and nothing written

programs.what: Gives the tentative size of a change, Small, Large or Not sized, against the work in progress now. A change is Large when a feature moves into or out of a piece in progress, when an EPIC gets more than one New story or Split, or when two or more pieces regroup.

the status lines of the things file, the data model files, the Feature catalog, the EPIC grouping, the FRDs and the Story lists

programs.name: `recommend.cjs`
programs.what: Writes the recommendation of a change: which workflows to run, from which steps, for which items. It also offers a small update when one fits, "Insert it" or "Copy the wording", and offers a re-run of the whole workflow when the change reaches more than half of the BRD's business requirements.
takesIn: the Change impact report: sections 5, 6, 7, 9, 13 and 14
the data model, when the project has one
givesOut: section 15 of the Change impact report, "The recommendation": the steps with their items, `park.cjs` first when the change is Large, your choices, and the one it recommends
inFlow: `change-impact-author`, after `size-rules.cjs` and before its gate, in step 5 of `requirement-update-workflow`
`track-change.cjs` loads it, to write a change's progress rows
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Only `change-impact-author` runs it, and the programs that load it use it only for a change.

programs.name: `check-change-report.cjs`
programs.what: Checks a Change impact report before the gate of `change-impact-author`, and prints the three blocks the gate needs. It checks every section, 1 to 16, and that the size and the recommendation are what `size-rules.cjs` and `recommend.cjs` give now.
givesOut: pass, or the problems found
the three blocks: For the person, One line, and For the file
inFlow: `change-impact-author`, after `recommend.cjs` and before its gate "Accept the recommendation, including the size?", in step 5 of `requirement-update-workflow`
programs.changeOnlyWhy: Only `change-impact-author` runs it.

programs.name: `insert-answer.cjs`
programs.what: Writes a late answer into every place the documents name its question, and changes nothing else. It refuses, and writes nothing, when any place would need other words changed.
takesIn: the answer, from the Question log
every document that names the question, the data model files among them
givesOut: the answer written in every place, with its source
each place recorded in the change's progress, under "Places written"
a new version of each accepted document it changed, through `accept.cjs`
or a refusal, with nothing written
inFlow: `requirement-update-workflow`, after you chose "Insert it" at the change's gate
`recommend.cjs` loads it, to name the places it would change
`copy-wording.cjs` loads it, to run `accept.cjs` the same way
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It runs only after you chose "Insert it" at a change's gate.

programs.name: `copy-wording.cjs`
programs.what: Copies a requirement's new wording to every place that quotes it: its row in the PRD and its line in each FRD's Requirements list. It refuses, and writes nothing, when a place does not hold the old wording word for word.
takesIn: the new wording, from section 5 of the Change impact report
the old wording, from the PRD
givesOut: the new wording in every place that quotes the requirement
each place recorded in the change's progress, under "Places written"
a new version of each accepted document it changed, through `accept.cjs`
or a refusal, with nothing written
inFlow: `requirement-update-workflow`, after you chose "Copy the wording" at the change's gate
`recommend.cjs` loads it, to name the places it would change
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It runs only after you chose "Copy the wording" at a change's gate.

programs.name: `close-change.cjs`
programs.what: Writes a change's closing entry once every document it named is accepted, and marks its progress closed. It refuses while any row of the progress is still pending.
takesIn: the Decision record of the first document in the progress, or the report's own
givesOut: the closing entry "Change {nnn} closed" in a Decision record
the progress marked "Status: closed on {date}"
or the pending rows listed
inFlow: `track-change.cjs`, when the last row of a change's progress is accepted
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It runs only to close a change.

programs.name: `lib/change-report.cjs`
programs.what: Reads a Change impact report into data, so every program reads its sections the same way. It gives each section the programs use, such as the asks, where they land, the kinds, the size and the choice at the gate.
givesOut: the report's sections as data
the five kinds, the update test's results and the judgements, as the report writes them
inFlow: loaded by `park.cjs`, which uses it only with a change
loaded by `track-change.cjs`, which uses it only for an open change
programs.changeOnlyWhy: It reads only Change impact reports. `park.cjs` and `track-change.cjs` load it, but use it only for an open change.
